messages:
marta: FYI bringing up MistralX-2 (internal 'turbine') on staging. Quick sanity check found a small token aliasing issue that cascades into KV-cache misalignment in long-context runs.
ben: can you paste a minimal repro/log?
marta: sure — tokenizer output vs expected for a short span:
```
text: "...financial-side-effects"
expected tokens: [31245, 4021, 199]
observed tokens: [31246, 4021, 199]  # +1 on the rare token id
```
jordan: that +1 smells like vocab-table offset/legacy-bpe mapping. we've seen vendor tokenizers that shipped with an extra sentinel id. Does it only hit rare emojis/punctuation?
marta: mostly rare ligatures and long hyphenated words. But when that +1 happens mid-sequence the KV cache rows shift (we index by token id in our adapter) so attention pulls the wrong K/V for later steps. Repro: run with context length 2048 and a prompt that includes the ligature -> you start getting token repeats ~50 tokens later.
carla: sample log of the repetition pattern?
marta: pasted small trace: 
```
step 120: input token id 31246 -> kv_index 31246 -> decoded token 'financial-'
step 171: attends to kv_index 31245 -> decoded token 'financial-' (repeats)
```
carla: ugh. That explains the KL spike in the evals. We saw a 0.18 -> 0.40 KL increase on the 1k prompt set after quantizing to 4-bit with the new runtime build. Might be compounded by rotary param mismatch.
eva: also saw p50 latency drop 7% but p99 regressed slightly after the quant build. Quality vs perf tradeoff looking worse because the token aliasing causes downstream generation loops.
ben: possible fixes: (1) remap table in tokenizer adapter to canonical ids (cheap), (2) change KV-indexing to use sequence-positioned cache instead of token-id keyed (bigger). For immediate safety, remap seems fastest.
jordan: agree. Also double-check rotary base/scale: some of these MistralX variants use scale factor ~1.00012 to keep numeric stability in headwise rope. If our compiled kernels assume 1.0 we can get phase-slip that amplifies with quant noise.
carla: patch idea: apply token_remap = { observed_id: canonical_id } in loader, add a flag "preserve_kv_by_pos" for risky models (off by default). Add unit test that does: random rare-token insertion -> run two inits -> assert KV equality.
marta: started branch: `ml/mistralx/alias-remap`. Quick perf that matters: baseline (hosted prod gemma 7B) p50=42ms p95=160ms; turbine staged (MistralX-2 8B quant4) p50=38ms p95=185ms but perplexity +12% on eval set. After local remap patch early run: p50 39ms p95 170ms, perplexity back in line (~+2%).
eva: numbers look promising. Can we run full eval (1k prompts, rouge/kl/bias checks) and a small canary on Dedicated pool?
deploy-bot: scheduled canary job #cj-881 on dedicated-pool-2 for branch ml/mistralx/alias-remap; will run nightly. ETA 12h.
ben: action items: 1) Marta finish remap list + unit tests, 2) Jordan vet rotary_scale param across model configs, 3) Carla run full eval and sanity CT (content tests), 4) Eva monitor canary metrics and abort thresholds: kl>0.1 or repeat-rate>0.02.
marta: on it. I'll drop PR when tests pass. Thanks all :thumbsup:
jordan: if the remap grows big we should script generation from tokenizer vocab diffs so it’s deterministic.
carla: good call. Also add a quick integration test that runs a short generation at 4-bit quant to catch regressions in CI.
eva: tagging infra: if canary hits regression, auto-rollback to last working runtime build and notify incident channel.
ben: note for postmortem: this wasn't caught earlier because unit tests used token-id stable subset; needs test coverage for rare-token paths.
marta: noted. will add tests and a short doc in the model onboarding checklist about token-aliasing checks.
carla: great. we should be able to have the canary results tomorrow morning.
deploy-bot: canary job started (cj-881). Logs will be available at https://ci.internal/redwood/cj-881
ben: thanks, closing loop for today.
